title: UFC Star Shares Shocking Reaction After Jailton Almeida Was Removed From The Promotion - NewsBreak
text:
By Pavan Sharma ,
1 hours ago
Jailton Almeida (Image Credits: Imagn) The UFC has recently made many shocking roster cuts . Now, a report suggests Jailton Almeida was removed from the company on February 11, 2026, despite him being ranked 8 in the heavyweight division. The promotion cut him after two consecutive lackluster performances, most recently a UFC loss to Rizvan Kuniev at UFC Vegas 113. After the report spread like wildfire, the fellow Brazilian fighter was super shocked.
Gilbert Burns reacted to the news, saying he‚Äôd like to see Almeida back at light heavyweight. That‚Äôs suggesting the weight class change could revive his career. In his words, ‚Äú Wow would like to see him back at 205 .‚Äù Burns‚Äô suggestion about 205 makes sense. Almeida might be struggling with the size and power of natural heavyweights. Dropping to light heavyweight could give him speed and cardio advantages.
His departure is notable, as he becomes the fourth top-15 heavyweight released in the past year. Jairzinho Rozenstruik, Martin Buday, and Alexandr Romanov were all cut previously.¬†The UFC‚Äôs willingness to release four ranked heavyweights in one year shows they‚Äôre prioritizing entertainment value over rankings integrity.
A Glimpse Of Jailton Almeida‚Äôs UFC Career Jailton Almeida (Image Credits: Imagn) Almeida finished his UFC run at 8-3, which is a winning record that makes his release even more surprising. He entered through Dana White‚Äôs Contender Series. His resume includes notable wins over Derrick Lewis, Jairzinho Rozenstruik, Serghei Spivac, and Alexandr Romanov.
Those are quality heavyweight victories that typically would keep you employed. He holds the UFC heavyweight record for 67.7% control time percentage, the highest in division history. His 22-5 overall MMA record shows legitimate skill, but his last few heavyweight fights cost him his job despite being ranked 8.
Now, as a free agent, Almeida can sign with Bellator, PFL, or another promotion. His record and ranking make him valuable elsewhere, even if the UFC didn‚Äôt want him, just as Muhammad Mokaev made his career in Brave CF .
